did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the beginning of the chapter, Ezra is introduced as the son of Seraiah, and the details of his genealogy begin here.
Did you know? Ezra’s genealogy traces back to Aaron the priest, who is called “the chief priest” in this verse.
Did you know? Ezra is described as “a skilled scribe in the Law of Moses”—that is, a scholar well versed in the Torah—and the king granted all his requests.
Did you know? Those who traveled with Ezra to Jerusalem included not only Israelites, but also priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants.
Did you know? Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the seventh year of King Artaxerxes’ reign.

Did you know? The journey from Babylon began on the first day of the first month and ended on the first day of the fifth month; the text attributes its success to “the good hand of his God” upon Ezra.
Did you know? Ezra committed himself to three things: studying the Law of the Lord, practicing it, and teaching its statutes and laws in Israel.
Did you know? The king’s decree allowed Ezra to bring to Jerusalem silver and gold donated by the king, his advisers, the people, and the priests.
Did you know? The money was intended to purchase bulls, rams, lambs, grain offerings, and drink offerings, and to offer them on the altar of the house of God in Jerusalem.
Did you know? Artaxerxes authorized Ezra to appoint judges and magistrates, teach the law of God, and judge anyone who did not obey the law of God or the law of the king.
